راتب.etymology: From the Arabic root ر ت ب, associated with being fixed or established. The adjective راتب can describe something regular or enduring; as a noun it names an employee’s pay for a specified period.
راتب.notes: The Cairo Academy records both the wage sense and the expression for a fixed, regular livelihood. This is a documented semantic connection, not a proposed date for the first use of salary. The lesson uses the noun meaning salary.

history.meaning: fixed or regular; salary paid for work

sources.title: Cairo Arabic Language Academy: رتب, especially الراتب and المرتب

مصروف.etymology: An Arabic formation from ص ر ف, a family which includes spending money. The shape مفعول is the passive-participle pattern; the noun مصروف denotes money for expenses or an allowance.
مصروف.notes: The Academy explicitly records صرف المال for spending money. The passive-pattern analysis explains the formation, while the allowance sense in this lesson is established by the original Saudi dialogue. It is not a claim that every occurrence means pocket money.

morphemes.meaning: passive-participle formation; not a separate suffix

rootFamily.gloss: spend money; also turn or redirect
currency exchange; morphology, in other contexts

sources.title: Cairo Arabic Language Academy: صرف, especially spending money and المصرف

شهري.etymology: A relational adjective formed from شهر, month, with the Arabic adjective-forming ending ي. The feminine singular form adds ة: شهرية.
شهري.notes: The Academy explicitly identifies الشهري as belonging to or derived from الشهر and records الشهرية for a payment fixed by month. This is month → monthly morphology; it does not imply every word in the broader root family has a time-related meaning.

sources.title: Cairo Arabic Language Academy: شهر, especially الشهر, الشهري and الشهرية

مسؤول.etymology: An Arabic passive-participle formation from سأل, ask or call someone to account. The accountability sense connects being responsible with having to answer for a person or matter.
مسؤول.notes: The Academy groups the responsible person under سأل and describes a duty whose consequences fall on that person. In this lesson مسؤول is an adjective; the related noun can mean an official. That noun sense must not replace the contextual gloss responsible.

morphemes.meaning: passive-participle formation: one who is answerable

sources.title: Cairo Arabic Language Academy: سأل, especially المسؤول and المسؤولية
